faq: Will imported orders send emails to customers?
No. We turn notifications off for the import and mark each order as historical. Customers see nothing, and stock levels are not reduced, so your live numbers stay correct.
Can customers see their old orders in their account?
That depends on the platform. Some link imported orders to the customer's account once they log in with the same email, others only show them to staff. We tell you which applies before we start.
Do payments and refunds get moved too?
We record the amounts and statuses so reports line up, but we cannot move actual payments or card data. Refunding an old order still happens in your previous payment provider's account.
How far back should I import?
Most stores import two to three years for support and tax questions and keep an archive file of the rest. We help you decide based on your order volume and the limits of the new platform.

desc:
Order history migration for ecommerce stores brings your past orders into the new store as historical records. Ecom Swift LLC exports, formats and imports them in your own account, then proves that the counts and totals match the old system.

## What is order history migration?

Order history migration is the transfer of completed orders from one store to another. Each order carries its items, quantities, totals, dates, addresses, status and often a tracking number. In the new store these appear as history: you can search them, link them to customers and use them for reports.

They are records, not live orders. They do not charge a card, send an email or reduce stock.

## Why old orders still matter

A customer writes in asking about a purchase from last spring. Without the order history you have to open the old platform, if you still have it, and hunt for the record. Once the old store is closed, that option disappears.

Past orders also support returns, warranty questions and accounting checks. They show which products sell, which customers come back and how seasons behave. Losing them means starting your reporting from a blank page.

## How order data helps support and decisions

Support speed depends on information being in one place. When history sits in the new store next to each customer record, an agent can answer a question in a minute instead of switching systems. Refund and exchange requests are easier to verify because the original order, discount and shipping line are visible.

For planning, a full history lets you see repeat buyers, average basket size and busy periods. These patterns guide stock buying and campaigns. The value comes from the data being accurate, which is why checking and reconciliation are part of the work.

## What a careful order import includes

- A complete export of orders from the old store, including statuses.
- Line items with product names, SKUs, quantities and prices.
- Order dates preserved, so reports show the real timeline.
- Billing and shipping addresses attached to each order.
- Links between each order and the matching customer record.
- Refunds, partial refunds, discount codes and shipping lines recorded.
- Tax lines and order notes carried over where the new platform supports them.
- Tracking numbers attached to shipped orders.
- Imports made without customer emails or stock changes.
- A reconciliation sheet comparing order counts and totals old versus new.

## What we do

We export the orders you want to keep and review the file for gaps, such as missing emails or products that no longer exist. We agree how far back to go. You can import everything or only the last few years.

We then map each field to the new platform and import a small batch first. We open those orders and compare them with the originals, line by line. When the sample is right, we load the rest in stages and mark the orders clearly as imported history.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of orders and in the detail carried across. Higher packages add refunds, tracking, tax lines, tags and a line-by-line check of sample orders, plus an archive of the original export for your records.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Import customers before orders, so orders can link to them.
- Keep a copy of the original export in a safe place.
- Decide how many years of history you really need.
- Check totals against your accounting records.
- Tell your support team where to find old orders.

**Avoid:**
- Importing orders with notifications switched on.
- Mixing test orders into the live history.
- Closing the old store before the reconciliation is signed off.
- Expecting payment records to move between providers.
- Assuming every platform stores every field in the same way.

## Who this is for

A shop that has traded for several years and answers questions about past purchases every week. A seller moving platforms who needs complete records for returns and tax. A business that runs reports on repeat buying and does not want a gap in the data.

## What we need from you

Give us an order export, or a staff or collaborator user on the old store so we can create one. Tell us how far back you want to go and whether you need refunds and tracking included.

No passwords are needed. We work in your accounts with limited access, and you can end that access when the import is approved.
